name: Bay State Eats: Massachusetts
subtitle: Clam Shacks, Roast Beef & More
description:
Massachusetts's restaurants, from the North Shore's roast beef stands to the clam shacks of Cape Ann and the Cape.

Bay State Eats is a free guide to eating in Massachusetts: 20 clam shacks and lobster roll stops, 5 North Shore roast beef shops, 19 North End Italian places, 11 Chinatown dim sum houses and bakeries, 8 classic diners, 4 Portuguese kitchens and 8 historic taverns and inns we checked by hand, plus 15,519 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 327 cities and towns, from Boston and Worcester to the Berkshires and the Islands. No account, no ads.

MASSACHUSETTS GUIDES
• Clam Shacks & Lobster Rolls: Cape Cod, Cape Ann and the South Shore.
• North Shore Roast Beef: the 3-way, from Revere to Peabody.
• North End Italian: trattorias, pastry shops and cannoli.
• Chinatown Dim Sum & Bakeries: Boston's Chinatown and Quincy.
• Classic Diners: Worcester's lunch cars and on.
• Portuguese and Historic Taverns & Inns.
• Oldest Places: 7 restaurants with a checked founding year.
• MICHELIN & James Beard: 45 honored Massachusetts restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "lobster roll", "roast beef revere", "dim sum".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 article, a visitor bureau's own guide or listing, or the MICHELIN Guide. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule tested where cities publish official restaurant lists. Cambridge publishes its food permits and sanitary inspections as open data, and Somerville its food permits and licenses; Cambridge's latest inspection appears on its places in the city's own words, dated, never as a grade. Boston's data portal can't be read by apps, so Boston places link the city's inspection search; elsewhere each place links the local board of health's search. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings, and the app computes no grades. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Bay State Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, any city or town, or Meet Boston or any visitor bureau), or with Michelin or the James Beard Foundation. MICHELIN and the MICHELIN Guide are trademarks of Michelin. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Bay State Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Massachusetts (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: clam shacks and lobster rolls, North Shore roast beef, North End Italian, Chinatown dim sum and bakeries, classic diners, Portuguese kitchens and historic taverns, 75 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the MICHELIN Guide and James Beard honorees. It also lists 15,519 restaurants, cafés and bars in 327 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Clam Shacks & Lobster Rolls (or North Shore Roast Beef, North End Italian, Portuguese, Classic Diners, Chinatown Dim Sum & Bakeries, Historic Taverns & Inns, MICHELIN & James Beard, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it; on Cambridge places an "Official inspection" section shows the city's latest record as the city words it, with its date, and a link opens the city's own inspection search in Safari.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("lobster roll", "roast beef revere", "dim sum").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Massachusetts (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Massachusetts, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Bay State Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Bay State Eats: Massachusetts".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Bay State Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the City of Cambridge's food permits and sanitary inspections (Open Data Commons PDDL) and the City of Somerville's permits and licenses (ODbL); MICHELIN Guide and James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and visitor bureau listings.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/massachusetts-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Massachusetts; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution and licenses on the About tab. Ratings, hours and photos are shown only inside Apple's own place card through MapKit; the app stores no ratings or reviews. Official inspection records are shown only as the city publishes them, labeled and dated; the app computes no grades. Every website link was checked before release, and adult venues are excluded. The app is independent and not affiliated with any restaurant, agency or award body.
